name: Jens Grede
profile: Swedish-born entrepreneur (b. 1978) who co-founded ad agencies Saturday Group and Wednesday (majority sold to BBDO in 2016), fashion label Frame (2012), and in 2019 SKIMS with Kim Kardashian and his wife Emma Grede. As CEO he and Kardashian hold a majority stake; SKIMS was valued at over $5B as of 2025.
interesting_fact: He left school in 1997 to become managing editor of the Stockholm magazine Stockholm New, before Tyler Brule recruited him to his London agency Winkreative in 2000.
deep_cut_fact: At Winkreative he worked on the rebrand of Swiss International Air Lines and helped design the fashion identity and logo for Stella McCartney's eponymous label; he also met future partner Erik Torstensson there.
notes: No published press email found on skims.com; company contact page is customer-service oriented. Son of Swedish film director Kjell Grede.

name: Saritha Katikaneni
current_role: Former co-founder and VP Marketing, Zenoti (Soham Inc.); current role not found
profile: Listed (Crunchbase, insider-data sites) as a co-founder and VP of Marketing of Zenoti, the Bellevue, WA salon/spa management software company founded in 2010 (legal name Soham Inc.), reportedly holding that role 2010-2019. Zenoti's current leadership page names Sudheer Koneru, Dheeraj Koneru and Anand Arvind as founders and does not mention her.
interesting_fact: Zenoti, founded in 2010, describes itself as the leading software platform for salons, spas, medspas and fitness brands and lists about 1,000 employees.
notes: Very low public profile; only directory sources (Crunchbase says she attended University of South Alabama and is Austin-based; unverified). Appears to have left Zenoti around 2019, so the company press email may not reach her.

name: Justin Woodward
current_role: Co-founder (tax attorney), Taxbit, Salt Lake City
profile: Utah tax attorney who co-founded Taxbit, the crypto/digital-asset tax and information-reporting software company, with his brother Austin Woodward (CPA, ex-Qualtrics) and cousin Brandon Woodward. Taxbit raised a $100M Series A in 2021 and became a unicorn, serving exchanges, enterprises and government agencies.
interesting_fact: His brother Austin calls him 'one of the youngest law grads at University of Chicago ever' and says Justin was already working on cryptocurrency tax issues for Fortune 500 companies in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: Before Taxbit he was a judicial law clerk for U.S. District Judge Dale Kimball (handling matters incl. cryptocurrency civil forfeiture) and earlier a 'Cyber Currencies Project Leader' at Kirkland & Ellis.
notes: media@taxbit.com is from a 2021 release; current press page only links a contact form. Has appeared on the Wharton FinTech podcast with Austin (2021).

name: Martin Traverso
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Starburst; co-founder, Trino Software Foundation
profile: Software engineer who co-created the Presto distributed SQL engine at Facebook with Dain Sundstrom, David Phillips and Eric Hwang after joining its data-infrastructure team in 2012. He co-founded Starburst, which commercialises Presto/Trino for querying data lakes and federated sources, and leads the open-source Trino project.
interesting_fact: Presto was built because Facebook's data scientists needed fast, accurate interactive queries over more than 300 petabytes of data spread across multiple databases.
deep_cut_fact: In January 2019 he, Sundstrom and Phillips forked Presto as 'PrestoSQL' and set up the not-for-profit Presto Software Foundation; in December 2020 the fork was rebranded Trino. Trino now underpins products like Amazon Athena.
notes: Technical founder, active in the Trino community (trino.io, Trino Slack). LinkedIn URL is what DataStax's podcast-guest page redirects to; not otherwise verified.

name: Max Bennett
current_role: Researcher (neural memory, cortical microcircuits) at Columbia University and the Astera Institute; author
profile: Former Goldman Sachs trader who in 2013 co-founded Bluecore (AI marketing personalisation for retailers, valued at $1B+) and served as its Chief Product Officer, then co-founded AI shopping-assistant company Alby; both were acquired. He wrote 'A Brief History of Intelligence' (Mariner, 2023) and now does neuroscience/AI research at Columbia and the Astera Institute.
interesting_fact: His book 'A Brief History of Intelligence' was called 'amazing' by Nobel laureate Daniel Kahneman; he gave a keynote at Cosyne 2025 and appeared on Armchair Expert with Dax Shepard.
deep_cut_fact: Despite no academic post at the time, he published peer-reviewed neuroscience papers, e.g. 'An Attempt at a Unified Theory of the Neocortical Microcircuit in Sensory Cortex' (Frontiers in Neural Circuits, 2020); he sits on the board of the Thousand Brains Project and is writing a sci-fi novel about the origins of life.
notes: Very approachable for an AI/brains podcast angle; frequent podcast guest. Lavin lists him as Forbes 30 Under 30.

name: Albert Chon
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Injective Labs (per available profiles; current status not confirmed)
profile: Stanford-trained computer scientist (BS in CS/AI, MS in CS/systems) and ex-Amazon engineer who co-founded Injective Labs with Eric Chen in 2018; Injective came out of Binance Labs' first incubation program. Injective is a Cosmos-SDK layer-1 blockchain for decentralised spot and derivatives trading, backed by Pantera, Jump Crypto and Mark Cuban.
interesting_fact: Injective Labs was part of the very first incubation program hosted by Binance Labs in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto, he was valedictorian at Gretchen Whitney High School, studied biotechnology at Penn's Summer Academy in Applied Science & Technology, and worked as an analytical chemist; he later did research at Stanford's Parallel Distributed Processing Lab (2016).
notes: Deep-cut details come from IQ.wiki (crypto encyclopedia citing his profile), not a primary source. No published press email found for Injective; Eric Chen is the public face of the company. No verified personal social accounts confirmed.

name: Jonas Diezun
profile: German serial founder (TU Munich business/electrical engineering, CDTM) who was an early team member helping scale rail-tech firm Konux, then in 2020 co-founded Berlin e-commerce aggregator Razor Group, which hit unicorn status in 2021. Since 2022 he runs Beam AI, which builds self-learning AI agents for enterprise workflows.
interesting_fact: Razor Group, which buys and scales Amazon marketplace brands, reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021, only about a year after he co-founded it.
deep_cut_fact: He studied behavioural economics and neuroscience at TU Munich and, by his own account, became a 'semi-professional pizza maker' during the pandemic; his Beam bio invites people to ask him about the best coffee spots in Munich.
notes: Now focused on AI agents (relevant to AI/data-center angle). Writes regularly on the Beam blog; LinkedIn is the most active channel.

name: Giles Andrews
current_role: Senior Independent Director, C. Hoare & Co.; NED Bank of Ireland Group; chair, carwow
profile: British fintech pioneer who in 2004 co-founded Zopa, the world's first online peer-to-peer lending platform (now a UK digital bank), serving as CEO 2007-2015 and chairman 2015-2019. He now sits on bank boards (C. Hoare & Co., Bank of Ireland), chairs car marketplace carwow and previously chaired MarketFinance. OBE for services to financial services.
interesting_fact: Before fintech he spent a decade in the motor industry, co-founding Caverdale in 1992 and growing it into a GBP250m-turnover motor retailer sold in 1997 - a car link that resurfaces in his chairmanship of carwow.
deep_cut_fact: He studied Psychology at Christ Church, Oxford, before an INSEAD MBA; after INSEAD his consultancy clients included Tesco and Tesco Personal Finance. He likes to 'search for the sun in the microclimate of the Isle of Wight'.

public_contacts.value: Champions Speakers / CSA speaker booking (speakers.co.uk enquiry form)

notes: No longer on Zopa's board page (2026). Named FinTech Leader of the Year at the 2016 FinTech Innovation Awards. Best route likely via speaker bureau or LinkedIn.

name: Alvin Tamsir
current_role: Scientific Fellow and Co-Founder, Pivot Bio (Berkeley, CA)
profile: Synthetic biologist (BA Molecular & Cell Biology, UC Berkeley; PhD UCSF under Christopher Voigt) who co-founded Pivot Bio in 2011 with lab mate Karsten Temme. Pivot Bio makes nitrogen-fixing microbes that replace part of farmers' synthetic fertiliser; Tamsir led its first commercial corn product, co-authored foundational patents and grew research from under 10 to 200+ scientists.
interesting_fact: Pivot Bio grew out of a 2011 paper by Temme and Dehua Zhao in Voigt's lab on engineering nitrogen fixation - an idea Berkeley dean Paul Ludden suggested to Voigt after a photosynthesis grant proposal was heavily criticised.
deep_cut_fact: As a PhD student he was first author of a 2010 Nature paper, 'Robust multicellular computing using genetically encoded NOR gates and chemical wires', building logic circuits out of communicating E. coli colonies.
notes: Scientist, low media profile; route via Pivot Bio media team. The source page renders the address as 'media@www.pivotbio.com' (CMS artifact); recent Business Wire releases reportedly use media@pivotbio.com.

name: Aron Schwarzkopf
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Kushki (Latin American payments infrastructure)
profile: Ecuadorian entrepreneur raised in Quito, educated at Babson College (also Singularity University and CUHK), now Miami-based. With Sebastian Castro he built and sold US fintech Leaf (2014), then founded Kushki, a payments acquirer/infrastructure company; its $186M Series B in 2022 made it Ecuador's first unicorn.
interesting_fact: Kushki means 'money' in Ecuadorian Kichwa; its 2022 Series B (Kaszek, SoftBank Latin America Fund, DILA, Clocktower) made it Ecuador's first-ever unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: He and co-founder Sebastian Castro, both from Ecuador, met in Boston as college students while watching soccer; he has said 'We never thought that we would return home' to build a company.
notes: Kushki site only publishes support/security emails (soporte@, seguridad@kushkipagos.com), not press. Listed in Bloomberg Linea 500 (2022) and has a World Economic Forum profile; LinkedIn likely best route.

name: Elik Eizenberg
current_role: Founder and CEO, Scroll AI (AI 'mentor' for employees); co-founder and former CTO, BigPanda
profile: Israeli technologist who co-founded BigPanda (AIOps / IT incident intelligence, backed by Sequoia) in 2012 with Assaf Resnick and served as CTO as it reached unicorn status. He has since founded Scroll AI, focused on reliable, ethical AI that acts as a trusted partner to human leaders.
interesting_fact: He describes 25 years of deploying mission-critical AI across finance, operations and security, and frames his mission around 'the humanist side of technology'.
deep_cut_fact: Before BigPanda he led development of highly scalable data pipelines in the Israeli intelligence service, then designed autonomous trading algorithms for a hedge fund - experiences that made him sceptical of ML vendor hype.
notes: Name sometimes spelled 'Eisenberg'. No published contact email found for Scroll AI; LinkedIn or Scroll's site are likely routes.
